academic_translation: This is because the present mind, too, is unapprehendable.
translation: This is because the present mind also cannot be found.

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: If someone were to completely fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give a gift, would that son of noble family or daughter of noble family produce much merit on that basis?
translation: If someone completely filled this universe of a billion worlds with the seven precious things and gave it as a gift, would that son of a good family or daughter of a good family make a lot of stored-up goodness from that?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: "Blessed One, it is much.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it is a lot.

academic_translation: Sugata, it is much."
translation: Well-Gone One, it is a lot."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, it is so; it is so.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, it is so. It is so."

academic_translation: That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would produce a great mass of merit on that basis.
translation: "That son of a good family or daughter of a good family would make a big pile of stored-up goodness from that."

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, if a mass of merit were a mass of merit, the Tathāgata would not speak of "a mass of merit, a mass of merit".
translation: "Also, Subhuti, if a pile of stored-up goodness were a pile of stored-up goodness, the Thus-Gone One would not speak of a 'pile of stored-up goodness, a pile of stored-up goodness.'"

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfect accomplishment of the form body?
translation: "Do you think the Thus-Gone One is seen by the full accomplishment of the form body?"

academic_translation: Subhūti said: Blessed One, it is not so.
translation: Subhuti said, "Blessed One, it is not so."

academic_translation: The Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfect accomplishment of the form body.
translation: The Thus-Gone One should not be seen by the full accomplishment of the form body.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because what is called the perfect accomplishment of the form body has been spoken of by the Tathāgata as no perfect accomplishment.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because the Thus-Gone One said that what is called the full accomplishment of the form body is no full accomplishment.

academic_translation: Therefore it is called the perfect accomplishment of the form body.
translation: That is why it is called the full accomplishment of the form body.

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: Do you think that the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?
translation: "Do you think the Thus-Gone One should be seen by perfect marks?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it is not so."

academic_translation: The Tathāgata is not to be viewed by the perfection of marks.
translation: You should not see the Thus-Gone One by his perfect marks.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because whatever perfection of marks the Tathāgata has spoken of, that has been spoken of by the Tathāgata as no perfection of marks.
translation: Why is that? Because whatever perfect marks the Thus-Gone One spoke of, the Thus-Gone One said they are not perfect marks.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called the perfection of marks.
translation: That is why they are called perfect marks.

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: If you think that the Tathāgata thinks, 'I have taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, do not view it in that way.
translation: If you think the Thus-Gone One thinks, 'I have given a teaching,' Subhuti, do not see it that way.

academic_translation: Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
translation: Because there is no thing at all that the Thus-Gone One has taught.

academic_translation: Subhūti, if anyone were to say this: 'The Tathāgata has taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, they would slander me by a mistaken grasping of what does not exist.
translation: Subhuti, if anyone says, 'The Thus-Gone One has taught a teaching,' they would be lying about me. They would be holding onto a mistake about something that does not exist.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'teaching the Dharma', it is because there is no Dharma whatsoever that can be apprehended as 'teaching the Dharma'.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, as for what is called 'explaining the teaching', there is no teaching at all that you can hold onto as 'explaining the teaching'.

academic_translation: Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
translation: Then the honored Subhuti said this to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: “Blessed One, in the future, will there be any sentient beings who, having heard such an explanation of the Dharma, will come to truly believe it?”
translation: "Blessed One, in the future, will there be any living beings who hear this explanation of the teaching and truly believe it?"

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: “Subhūti, they are neither sentient beings, nor are they not sentient beings.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, they are neither living beings, nor are they not living beings.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called 'sentient beings,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught that they are not sentient beings.”
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, as for what are called 'living beings,' it is because the Thus-Gone One has taught that they are not living beings."

academic_translation: Therefore, they are called sentient beings.
translation: That is why they are called living beings.

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as the unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?
translation: Do you think there is any thing the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to as the highest, complete awakening?

academic_translation: The venerable Subhūti said, Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as the unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: The honored Subhuti said, "Blessed One, there is no thing the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to as the highest, complete awakening."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, it is so. It is just so."

academic_translation: Therein, not even the slightest phenomenon is apprehended or exists.
translation: In it, not even the smallest thing is found or exists.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: That is why it is called the highest, complete awakening.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, that phenomenon is equal;
translation: Also, Subhuti, that thing is equal.

academic_translation: Since there is nothing whatsoever unequal or equal in it, therefore it is called unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: Because there is nothing unequal or equal in it, it is called the highest, complete awakening.

academic_translation: That unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening is equal in being without a self, without a sentient being, without a life-force, and without a person;
translation: That highest, complete awakening is equal because it is without a self, without a living being, without a life, and without a person.

academic_translation: it is fully awakened to by means of all virtuous phenomena.
translation: You become fully awake to it through all good things.
